stem: A visible nutrient-like symptom improves after correcting uneven irrigation without changing fertilizer concentration. What conclusion is best supported?
choices: Root-zone water distribution likely contributed to the symptom and nutrient availability or uptake problem
Visual symptoms can never involve nutrients
All future nutrient-like symptoms should be treated only with irrigation changes
rationale: Irrigation distribution affects root activity and root-zone chemistry. Improvement after correcting water distribution supports a root-zone contribution without proving that all similar symptoms share the same cause.
